source.title: Gradient Diversity Empowers Distributed Learning
source.authors: Dong Yin; A. Pananjady; Maximilian Lam; Dimitris Papailiopoulos; K. Ramchandran; P. Bartlett

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper; no material problem noted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares mini-batch sizes and reports training and test error behavior, using stability analysis and generalization plots rather than the original studies' methods.
record.gate_note: The large-batch stability experiment reports normalized model distance and generalization behavior. Figure 4 provides no recoverable numerical values for the training/test-error curves; cited results from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: Section 6.2 compares actual training and test errors for CIFAR-10 networks at batch sizes 512 and 1024, bearing on V5. However, the supplied figure text does not reveal the curves, and the verbal finding of greater variability does not establish worse held-out performance at a fixed epoch budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate but needs qualification: convergence guarantees cover convex and nonconvex objectives, whereas the stability-based generalization guarantees require convex, Lipschitz, smooth losses and appropriate batch sizes and step sizes. The CIFAR-10 experiment reports reduced parameter stability and greater variability in generalization behavior for larger batches.
record.recipe_differences: Compares mini-batch sizes and generalization behavior, but does not test the original large-batch generalization-gap methods or establish the fixed-epoch held-out accuracy claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes normalized model distance and the variance of generalization behavior in the reported experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Normalized model distance increases with batch size after replacing one training example.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger mini-batches reduce parameter stability in this CIFAR-10 experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report greater variability in generalization behavior for large batches, without stating a direction for held-out error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large batches produce more variable generalization trajectories in this experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: For convex losses under differential-gradient-diversity and step-size conditions, mini-batch SGD retains serial SGD's order of generalization-error bound.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Differential gradient diversity permits larger batches while preserving theoretical stability-based generalization guarantees for convex objectives.

record.problems: The neural-network generalization outcomes are presented only in plots without recoverable numerical values. The text reports higher variance, not a specific direction or magnitude of held-out error change. The experiment averages over 3 runs, with no error bars or other uncertainty estimates stated in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported result rows were omitted. The comparison in Section 6.1 concerns convergence loss ratios, not the held-out generalization outcomes named by the versions.

Language models and the effects of longer training, warmup, normalization or regularization changes on held-out performance. No readable fixed-epoch test-error ordering or small-batch held-out reference is supplied.
Dropout's effect on held-out error; the dropout experiments measure convergence loss ratios.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations and their ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict label is justified by the readable evidence: unavailable curve values are not evidence of an absent effect. The convex generalization bounds concern train-population risk discrepancies, not demonstrated held-out accuracy equality for image classifiers. Section 6.1 reports optimization outcomes, and the introduction's worse-generalization statement cites prior work.

Network width beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.

The paper's stated generalization result is higher variance, which does not establish the version's worse-held-out-performance claim.

rows.note: The text states that normalized distance becomes larger as batch size increases. This measures stability, not a claim version's named generalization outcome.
rows.check: The stated increase in normalized model distance measures sensitivity to replacing one training example, not V5's held-out performance penalty. Its direction is reported verbally, although numerical values are unavailable.
